finding.shortLabel: The unknown-corridor residual: eliminating named households does not clear the record's gaps

sources.locator: The forty-plus distinct John Gurney heads of household, England 1600–1670
Seven distinct John Gurneys fixed in England after 1637 by PCC probate

finding.statement: Eliminating named households is not the same as clearing the record. The same-name sweeps found more than forty distinct John Gurney heads of household in England between 1600 and 1670, and English parish-register coverage for the period is patchy enough that others existed unrecorded. The 1662-1666 London hearth-tax cluster makes the point concrete: eleven Gurney households in London alone, none of them surfaced by any candidate search, because a search built around a name, a wife, and a child set cannot see a household the registers never entered. The identity case file expresses this same residual as its two unknown-corridor scenarios, and it is the principal reason the estimate for Candidate B sits in the sixties rather than the nineties.

finding.shortLabel: Eleven Gurney households in the London hearth-tax returns, 1662-1666

sources.alignmentNote: Underlying manuscripts in TNA E 179. The 1662 St Augustine Watling Street entry in the same database is Candidate D's and is carried on G13-RI-000122, not here.
sources.locator: London Hearth Tax project database (Merry 2010), published with London Hearth Tax: City of London and Middlesex, 1666 and London Hearth Tax: Westminster 1664 - eleven strict Gurney/Gurny entries 1662-1666, incl. Walter Gurney (St Margaret's Westminster, Greene Dragon Court, 1 hearth, 1664), William Gurny (St Bride Fleet Street, 7 hearths, 1666, "empty"), William Gurney (St Dunstan in the West, Cock & Key Alley, 3 hearths, 1666), Ann Gurney (St Dunstan in the West, Two Crane Court, 5 hearths, 1666).

finding.statement: The London hearth-tax returns of 1662-1666 record eleven strict Gurney or Gurny household entries across the City of London, Westminster, and inner Middlesex. Among them: Walter Gurney at Greene Dragon Court in St Margaret's Westminster, 1 hearth, 1664; William Gurny on the south side of Fleet Street in St Bride's, 7 hearths, 1666, returned empty; William Gurney at Cock and Key Alley in St Dunstan in the West, 3 hearths, 1666; and Ann Gurney at Two Crane Court in the same parish, 5 hearths, 1666. All post-date the colonial John's death; none is a candidate for him.
